chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, from some of his men, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If it reaches you that your master has undergone a disappearance (ghaybah), do not deny it.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about denying the Imam's disappearance?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) serves as a foundational proof for the legitimacy of the Minor and Major Occultations, instructing believers to accept the Imam's absence as a divine decree rather than a contradiction. It emphasizes that the occultation is a known reality of the Imam's station, thereby countering early skeptics who questioned his presence. This instruction underscores the necessity of steadfastness (istiqama) in faith during periods of hidden leadership.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (42) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from some of his companions from Ahmad bin Muhammad from Ali bin al-Hakam from Abu Ayyoob al-Khazzaz from Muhammad bin Muslim

that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “If you are informed that your man has disappeared, do not deny that.” The same was narrated by Muhammad bin Ya’qoob from Ali bin Ibraheem bin Hashim from Muhammad bin Abu Omayr from Abu Ayyoob al-Khazzaz from Muhammad bin Muslim.
